## Purpose and Scope This document provides a high-level overview of the OpenCode codebase, describing its purpose as an open-source AI coding agent, the monorepo structure, core architecture patterns, and key capabilities. For detailed information about specific subsystems, see: - Repository structure and package dependencies: [Repository Structure & Packages](#1.1) - Detailed architecture diagrams: [Architecture Overview](#1.2) - Core application components: [Core Application](#2) - User interface implementations: [User Interfaces](#3) - SDK and API details: [SDK & API](#5) --- ## What is OpenCode OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent that provides a flexible alternative to proprietary AI code assistants like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot. It emphasizes provider-agnostic support, integrating with over 20 LLM providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini/Vertex, Amazon Bedrock, and local models such as Ollama and llama.cpp. The design prioritizes extensibility, user control, and open-source transparency. Key characteristics include: - **Open source**: Licensed under MIT, the entire platform is fully open source and community driven. [packages/opencode/package.json:6-6]() - **Provider-agnostic**: Unified integration layer supports dozens of LLM providers and allows pluggable authentication and model selection. [packages/opencode/package.json:58-76]() - **Multiple interfaces**: Offers Terminal UI (TUI), desktop apps (Electron/Tauri), IDE extensions (VS Code, Zed), and a web-based documentation site. [packages/desktop/package.json:1-76](), [packages/web/package.json:1-44]() - **LSP Integration**: Built-in Language Server Protocol support for 20+ languages provides semantic code intelligence. [packages/opencode/package.json:146-146]() - **Client-server architecture**: Core server can run locally or remotely, with a rich TypeScript SDK for interaction. [packages/sdk/js/package.json:12-21]() OpenCode aims to be a turnkey AI code assistant platform for developers and teams who want customizable AI-guided coding tools outside of vendor lock-in. This document describes the monorepo organization of the OpenCode repository, including workspace structure, package categories, and inter-package dependencies. OpenCode uses Bun workspaces to manage multiple packages that together provide CLI tools, desktop applications, web interfaces, IDE extensions, and a managed cloud platform. For information about the architectural patterns and runtime behavior of these systems, see [Architecture Overview](#1.2). --- ## Workspace Organization OpenCode is organized as a monorepo with workspaces defined in the root configuration [bun.lock:4-28](). The repository contains 20+ packages distributed across several directories: | Directory | Purpose | Package Count | |---|---|---| | `packages/` | Core platform, UI components, SaaS Console, and services | 15+ packages | | `sdks/` | IDE integrations and extensions | 2+ packages | | Root | Main CLI package and build tooling | Workspace root | ### Workspace Configuration The root workspace [bun.lock:5-29]() defines shared dependencies and catalog versions that child packages inherit. The catalog system enforces consistent versioning across all packages for critical dependencies such as `typescript`, `solid-js`, `zod`, and others. ### Repository Package Hierarchy Diagram ```mermaid graph TB Root["Root Workspace
(opencode)"] subgraph "packages/" Core["Core Platform
opencode, sdk, plugin,
script, core, llm, cli, server, protocol, schema, client, tui"] UI["UI Layer
app, ui, web, session-ui"] Desktop["Desktop Apps
desktop"] Console["Console Platform
console-core, console-app,
console-function, console-mail,
console-resource"] Services["Services & Integrations
function, slack, enterprise, http-recorder, effect-drizzle-sqlite, codemode"] end subgraph "sdks/" VSCode["vscode Extension"] end Root --> Core Root --> UI Root --> Desktop Root --> Console Root --> Services Root --> VSCode ``` ### Workspace Dependencies Packages reference each other using the `workspace:*` protocol [packages/opencode/package.json:90-92](), which Bun resolves to local package paths during development and proper versions during publishing. Sources: [bun.lock:1-29](), [packages/opencode/package.json:90-92]() --- ## Core Platform Packages These form the foundational software that powers OpenCode’s CLI, SDK, plugins, and core runtime functionality. ### opencode **Location**: `packages/opencode/` **Package Name**: `opencode` **Type**: Main CLI application and server runtime The main package of OpenCode containing the server logic, CLI commands, the tool system, session/agent management, and integrations with numerous LLM providers [packages/opencode/package.json:1-155](). This package represents the legacy monolithic core, with functionality gradually being migrated to more granular packages like `@opencode-ai/core`, `@opencode-ai/server`, `@opencode-ai/cli`, and `@opencode-ai/tui`. **Implementation Highlights**: - Provides the executable CLI binary at `bin/opencode` [packages/opencode/package.json:18-20]() - Implements an HTTP server built using the Hono framework. - Manages a tool registry and execution engine to run code and scripts. - Integrates and manages LSP servers (across 20+ languages). - Hosts session lifecycle and message part management, enabling AI agent workflows. - Provider integrations for 20+ LLM services including OpenAI, Anthropic, and OpenCode's Zen/Go runtimes [packages/opencode/package.json:58-94](). - Uses `drizzle-orm` for database abstractions [packages/opencode/package.json:117](). **Key Dependencies**: - AI SDKs: `ai`, `@ai-sdk/*` (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) [packages/opencode/package.json:60-76]() - Effect functional runtime: `effect`, `@effect/platform-node` [packages/opencode/package.json:80, 118]() - UI framework dependencies utilized internally: `solid-js`, `@opentui/solid` [packages/opencode/package.json:101, 138]() - Database ORM: `drizzle-orm` [packages/opencode/package.json:117]() ### @opencode-ai/cli **Location**: `packages/cli/` **Package Name**: `@opencode-ai/cli` **Type**: CLI Entrypoint This package is part of the v2 architecture, providing a standalone CLI entrypoint that orchestrates other v2 packages like `@opencode-ai/server` and `@opencode-ai/tui` [bun.lock:93-117](). It aims to replace the CLI functionality within the monolithic `opencode` package. **Details**: - Defines the CLI binary with an executable wrapper `bin/lildax.cjs` [bun.lock:97-98]() - Depends on `@opencode-ai/core` for domain logic, `@opencode-ai/sdk` for client communication, `@opencode-ai/server` for server functionality, and `@opencode-ai/tui` for the terminal UI [bun.lock:100-104](). - Uses the `effect` library to structure command handling and effects [bun.lock:108](). ### @opencode-ai/sdk **Location**: `packages/sdk/js/` **Package Name**: `@opencode-ai/sdk` **Type**: JavaScript SDK The official JavaScript SDK for OpenCode that enables client-side apps and IDE extensions to communicate with OpenCode servers [packages/sdk/js/package.json:1-35](). It provides both a legacy API and a v2 API designed for the new architecture. **Exports**: - Main module entrypoint (`./src/index.ts`) [packages/sdk/js/package.json:13]() - Client utilities (`./src/client.ts`) for creating clients with various transport modes [packages/sdk/js/package.json:14]() - Server utilities (`./src/server.ts`) for server-side integration [packages/sdk/js/package.json:15]() - V2 API with OpenAPI code generation support (`./src/v2/*`) supporting advanced schema-first client/server development [packages/sdk/js/package.json:16-20](). ### @opencode-ai/plugin **Location**: `packages/plugin/` **Package Name**: `@opencode-ai/plugin` **Type**: Plugin API and SDK Defines the API and infrastructure needed to create OpenCode plugins and custom tools [packages/plugin/package.json:1-54](). This document provides a high-level overview of the OpenCode system architecture, describing how the core components interact to provide an AI-powered coding assistant. It focuses on the backend infrastructure, API layers, core runtime components, and the transition toward the V2 architecture design across the monorepo packages. ## System Overview OpenCode is built as a modular, event-driven system centered around the `opencode` package that manages AI sessions, executes tools, and exposes a REST API. The architecture is deeply integrated with the `effect` library to manage side effects, dependency injection, and concurrency. This approach provides reliable orchestration of AI model calls, session management, and tool execution. The main runtime and services are implemented as `Effect` layers. In the current system, these are defined in `packages/opencode/src/effect/app-runtime.ts`, where services like `Session`, `Config`, `LLM`, and `ToolRegistry` are composed into a global `AppLayer` [packages/opencode/src/effect/app-runtime.ts:58-109](). The Core Application is the main OpenCode server package ([packages/opencode]()) that provides the foundational AI agent capabilities. It implements an Effect-based server with an embedded CLI interface, managing AI conversations (sessions), tool execution, provider integrations, and real-time event streaming. The server can run in-process (local mode) or as a networked service (remote mode), exposing an OpenAPI-compliant REST API. For detailed documentation of specific subsystems, see the related child pages: - [CLI Entrypoint & Commands](#2.1) - [Configuration System](#2.2) - [Session & Agent System](#2.3) - [AI Provider & Model Management](#2.4) - [Tool System & Permissions](#2.5) - [HTTP Server & REST API](#2.6) - [Event Bus & Real-time Updates](#2.7) - [LSP & Code Formatting](#2.8) - [Plugin System](#2.9) - [MCP Integration](#2.10) - [Skills & Command System](#2.11) - [ACP (Agent Client Protocol)](#2.12) - [LLM Core Library](#2.13) - [Core V2 Library (packages/core)](#2.14) - [Schema, Protocol & Client Packages](#2.15) --- ## Architecture Overview The Core Application follows a layered architecture organized via the **Effect** library to model side effects and async services. It utilizes a comprehensive `AppLayer` that merges all necessary service implementations, including filesystem utilities, database access, git integration, and session management. The `AppLayer` is defined in [packages/opencode/src/effect/app-runtime.ts:58-109]() and includes services like `Config`, `Auth`, `Session`, `ToolRegistry`, and `Project`. ### High-Level Architecture Diagram ```mermaid graph TB subgraph "Entrypoints" CLI["CLI Entry

It parses commands using `yargs`, sets environment flags (like `OPENCODE_PURE` or `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL`), and initializes the `Heap` snapshot system [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:33-78](). Commands are built using `effectCmd`, which provides an `InstanceStore` for managing project-specific state [packages/opencode/src/cli/effect-cmd.ts:69-96](). This utility ensures that project contexts are loaded and disposed of correctly, wrapping handlers in tracing spans [packages/opencode/src/cli/effect-cmd.ts:52-68](). The `InstanceBootstrap` service ([packages/opencode/src/project/bootstrap.ts]()) orchestrates the initialization of core services like `Config`, `Plugin`, `LSP`, `ShareNext`, `Snapshot`, `Vcs`, and `Project` for each instance [packages/opencode/src/project/bootstrap.ts:33-46](). ### Initialization Sequence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CLI as "index.ts" participant Yargs as "yargs" participant Middleware as "CLI Middleware" participant Heap as "Heap" participant Command as "CLI Command" participant AppRuntime as "AppRuntime" participant InstanceBootstrap as "InstanceBootstrap" participant Config as "Config.Service" participant Plugin as "Plugin.Service" participant LSP as "LSP.Service" participant OtherServices as "Other Services" CLI->>Yargs: parse(process.argv) Yargs->>Middleware: execute Middleware->>Heap: start() Middleware->>Command: execute Command->>AppRuntime: runPromise(Effect) AppRuntime->>InstanceBootstrap: run() InstanceBootstrap->>Config: get() InstanceBootstrap->>Plugin: init() InstanceBootstrap->>LSP: init() InstanceBootstrap->>OtherServices: init() OtherServices-->>InstanceBootstrap: initialized LSP-->>InstanceBootstrap: initialized Plugin-->>InstanceBootstrap: initialized Config-->>InstanceBootstrap: initialized InstanceBootstrap-->>AppRuntime: ready AppRuntime-->>Command: result Command-->>CLI: exit ``` Sources: [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:33-142](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/effect-cmd.ts:70-96](), [packages/opencode/src/project/bootstrap.ts:18-49]() --- ## CLI Interface & Commands Overview The CLI acts as the primary interface for both users and IDE integrations. It supports interactive modes (TUI), headless server modes, and programmatic task execution. For details, see [CLI Entrypoint & Commands](#2.1). | Command | Description | Key File Location | | :------ | :---------- | :---------------- | | `run` | Runs a message/task against an agent [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:126-128]() | `cli/cmd/run.ts` | | `tui` | Starts the interactive Terminal UI [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:72-74]() | `cli/cmd/tui.ts` | | `serve` | Starts a headless HTTP server [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts:6-9]() | `cli/cmd/serve.ts` | | `web` | Starts server and opens the web interface [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/web.ts:31-34]() | `cli/cmd/web.ts` | | `acp` | Starts the Agent Client Protocol server [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:9-11]() | `cli/cmd/acp.ts` | | `attach` | Connects a terminal to a running server [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:99-105]() | `cli/cmd/attach.ts` | The `run` command supports three primary modes: non-interactive (single prompt), interactive local (`--mini`), and interactive attach (`--attach`) [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:5-11](). The `Config.Service` ([packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts]()) is responsible for loading, merging, and updating configuration from various locations. It supports remote configurations, global user settings, project-specific `opencode.json` files, and managed system-level configurations. For details, see [Configuration System](#2.2). 1. **Remote config**: Organizational defaults from `.well-known/opencode` [packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx:63-65](). The `substituteWellKnownRemoteConfig` function in `Config.Service` handles fetching and substituting variables in remote configurations [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:64-98](). 2. **Global config**: User preferences in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` [packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx:99-101](). The `globalConfigFile()` function determines the path to the global configuration file [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:139-147](). 3. **Project config**: Local `opencode.json` in the project root [packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx:109-111](). 4. **Managed config**: System-level admin settings (e.g., `/etc/opencode/` or macOS MDM) [packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx:154-172](). For details, see [HTTP Server & REST API](#2.6) and [ACP (Agent Client Protocol)](#2.12). - **HTTP REST API**: Handled by the `Server` module ([packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts]()), providing OpenAPI-compliant routes [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts:14-20](). The `openapi()` function can generate the OpenAPI specification [packages/opencode/src/server/server.ts:67-69](). - **ACP (Agent Client Protocol)**: A JSON-RPC over stdio protocol for IDEs like Zed, implemented using `ndJsonStream` [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:55-61](). - **TUI Worker**: The TUI runs in a separate `Worker` process, communicating via RPC to maintain a responsive interface [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:210-216](). ### Bridging Natural Language Space & Code Entities: Transport Modes ```mermaid graph LR subgraph "Natural Language Space" User["User Prompt"] TUI["TUI (packages/tui)"] Zed["Zed IDE"] end subgraph "Code Entity Space (packages/opencode)" RunCmd["RunCommand

This page provides an in-depth technical overview of the OpenCode CLI entrypoint, its command routing system, argument parsing, and bootstrap process. It explains the command implementations, middleware pipeline, and error handling mechanisms. The focus is on the code-level understanding of how the CLI operates and delegates to specific commands such as `run`, `tui`, `serve`, `web`, `acp`, and others. For detailed documentation on the user-facing Terminal UI (TUI) application, refer to [Terminal User Interface (TUI)](/3.1). For HTTP server functionality underpinning `serve` and `web`, see [HTTP Server & REST API](/2.6). For configuration details, see [Configuration System](/2.2). --- ## Entrypoint Architecture The core CLI entrypoint is `packages/opencode/src/index.ts`, which uses the `yargs` library for parsing command-line arguments, registering commands, and managing global options [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:1-45](). ### High-Level Flow Title: CLI Execution Pipeline ```mermaid graph TB Entry["index.ts Entrypoint"] Yargs["yargs CLI parser"] Middleware["Middleware pipeline"] Commands["Registered Commands"] ErrorHandler["Global error handler"] Entry --> Yargs Yargs --> Middleware Middleware --> Commands Commands --> ErrorHandler Middleware --> HeapStart["Heap.start()"] Commands --> Run["RunCommand (run)"] Commands --> TuiThread["TuiThreadCommand (tui)"] Commands --> Serve["ServeCommand (serve)"] Commands --> Web["WebCommand (web)"] Commands --> Acp["AcpCommand (acp)"] Commands --> Github["GithubCommand (github)"] Commands --> Other["Other commands..."] ErrorHandler --> FormatError["FormatError()"] ErrorHandler --> Exit["process.exit()"] ``` This architecture initializes the CLI parser, sets up global middleware for environment configuration, registers all commands, and gracefully handles errors to provide helpful user feedback. Sources: [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:1-142]() --- ## CLI Parser Configuration The `yargs` parser is configured with various global settings to control how the CLI behaves and outputs help/version information [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:45-52](). | Setting | Value | Description | |---|---|---| | `scriptName` | `"opencode"` | Command name shown in help and usage text | | `wrap` | `100` | Wrap width for help text | | `parserConfiguration` | `{ "populate--": true }` | Support for `--` as argument separator | | `help`, `-h`, `--help` | Enabled | Displays help and usage information | | `version`, `-v`, `--version` | `InstallationVersion` (string) | Shows the CLI version | **Global options** available for all commands: | Option | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | `--print-logs` | boolean | Print log messages to stderr | | `--log-level` | string | Set log verbosity (DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) | | `--pure` | boolean | Run CLI without loading external plugins | Sources: [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:53-65]() --- ## Middleware Pipeline Before any command executes, middleware runs to initialize heap profiling and set environment variables relevant to agent operation. Title: CLI Middleware Initialization ```mermaid graph LR Start["Command invoked"] HeapStart["Heap.start(): Start memory monitoring"] EnvVars["Setup environment variables (AGENT, OPENCODE flags)"] Execute["Execute chosen command handler"] Start --> HeapStart HeapStart --> EnvVars EnvVars --> Execute ``` ### Middleware Details - **Logging Setup**: Initializes logging based on CLI flags like `--print-logs` and `--log-level`. [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:66-68]() - **Heap Tracking**: Starts memory heap tracking for diagnostics via `Heap.start()` [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:73-74](). - **Environment Variables**: Sets process-level environment variables: - `AGENT=1` - `OPENCODE=1` - `OPENCODE_PID` to the current process ID [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:75-77]() - `OPENCODE_PURE=1` if the `--pure` flag is present [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:69-71]() Sources: [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:66-78](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/heap.ts:1-10]() --- ## Command Registration & Dispatch ### Commands Overview Commands are registered as separate objects imported from `./cli/cmd/*`. Flow Diagrams ### Natural Language Space to CLI Command This diagram associates natural language commands with their CLI entrypoints and the key files implementing them. Title: CLI Command Resolution Map ```mermaid graph TD NLP["Command entered by user"] NLP -->|opencode run| RunCmd["RunCommand"] NLP -->|opencode serve| ServeCmd["ServeCommand"] NLP -->|opencode web| WebCmd["WebCommand"] NLP -->|opencode acp| AcpCmd["AcpCommand"] NLP -->|opencode github| GithubCmd["GithubCommand"] NLP -->|opencode tui| TuiCmd["TuiThreadCommand"] NLP -->|opencode attach| AttachCmd["AttachCommand"] NLP -->|opencode agent| AgentCmd["AgentCommand"] NLP -->|opencode models| ModelsCmd["ModelsCommand"] NLP -->|opencode plugin| PluginCmd["PluginCommand"] RunCmd --> FileRun["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts"] ServeCmd --> FileServe["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts"] WebCmd --> FileWeb["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/web.ts"] AcpCmd --> FileAcp["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts"] GithubCmd --> FileGithub["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/github.ts"] TuiCmd --> FileTui["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts"] AttachCmd --> FileAttach["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/attach.ts"] AgentCmd --> FileAgent["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/agent.ts"] ModelsCmd --> FileModels["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/models.ts"] PluginCmd --> FilePlugin["packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/plug.ts"] ``` Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:126](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts:6](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/web.ts:31](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:9](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/github.ts:37](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:1](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/attach.ts:1](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/agent.ts:1](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/models.ts:1](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/plug.ts:1]() --- ## Selected Command Details ### RunCommand (`opencode run`) `RunCommand` is the primary interface for non-interactive and interactive prompt execution. It supports three distinct modes [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:5-11](): 1. **Non-interactive**: Sends a single prompt and streams events to stdout. 2. **Interactive local**: Boots an in-process server with a split-footer UI (`--mini`). 3. **Interactive attach**: Connects to an existing remote server (`--attach`). Key options include: - `--model` / `-m`: Specify `provider/model` [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:165-169](). - `--agent`: Select specific agent configuration [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:170-173](). - `--file` / `-f`: Attach files to the message [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:180-185](). - `--format`: Choose between `default` (formatted) or `json` (raw events) [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:174-179](). The command implements custom tool rendering, using `toolInlineInfo` to display tool execution status with icons (e.g., `⚙` for general tools, `✗` for failures) [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:90-124](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run.ts:1-230]() ### Serve & Web Commands Both `ServeCommand` and `WebCommand` initialize an OpenCode server. - `serve`: Starts a headless server listening on a specified port [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts:6-23](). - `web`: Starts the server and automatically opens the web interface in the default browser using the `open` package [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/web.ts:31-84](). These commands utilize `resolveNetworkOptions` to parse hostname, port, and mDNS settings [packages/opencode/src/cli/web.ts:43](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/serve.ts:18](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/serve.ts:1-25](), [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/web.ts:31-85]() ### AcpCommand (`opencode acp`) The `AcpCommand` implements the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) server. It bridges JSON-RPC over `stdin`/`stdout` to an internal OpenCode server instance [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:9-73](). Implementation steps: 1. Starts the internal `Server` via `Server.listen(opts)` [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:25](). 2. Creates an `OpencodeClient` pointing to the local server [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:27-30](). 3. Wraps `process.stdin` and `process.stdout` into a `ndJsonStream` [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:32-55](). 4. Initializes `ACP.init` with the SDK and creates an `AgentSideConnection` [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:56-61](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/acp.ts:1-74]() ### StatsCommand (`opencode stats`) The `StatsCommand` aggregates and displays token usage and cost statistics from the local database [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/stats.ts:49-51](). - **Aggregation**: It queries the `SessionTable` via `Database.Service` to calculate totals for sessions, messages, costs, and token types (input, output, reasoning, cache) [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/stats.ts:83-147](). - **Filtering**: Supports filtering by `days` (e.g., last 30 days) and `project` [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/stats.ts:53-68](). - **Model Breakdown**: Can show top-N model usage including per-model cost and token metrics [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/stats.ts:184-203](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/stats.ts:1-230]() ### TuiThreadCommand (`opencode tui` or `opencode`) The `TuiThreadCommand` is responsible for launching the Terminal User Interface (TUI). When `opencode` is run without any arguments, it defaults to starting the TUI [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:8-10](). The TUI provides an interactive environment for working with an LLM, including features like file references (`@`), bash commands (`!`), and various slash commands (e.g., `/help`, `/new`, `/sessions`) [packages/web/src/content/docs/tui.mdx:30-282](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts:1](), [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:8-45](), [packages/web/src/content/docs/tui.mdx:1-282]() ### AgentCommand (`opencode agent`) The `AgentCommand` provides subcommands for managing AI agents, specifically `create` and `list` [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:55-61](). - **`opencode agent create`**: This command guides the user through creating a new agent with custom configuration. It prompts for a description, determines the storage scope (global or project), generates an agent configuration using an LLM, allows selection of permissions, and sets the agent mode (primary, subagent, or all) [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/agent.ts:33-210](). The agent configuration is saved as a Markdown file with frontmatter [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/agent.ts:208-210](). - **Permissions**: Agents are configured at the permission level (e.g., `bash`, `read`, `edit`), which maps to multiple tools [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/agent.ts:19-31](). - **Non-interactive mode**: All options (`--path`, `--description`, `--mode`, `--permissions`) can be provided as flags for non-interactive agent creation [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/agent.ts:78-79](). - **`opencode agent list`**: Lists all available agents [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:89-91](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/agent.ts:1-210](), [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:55-91](), [packages/web/src/content/docs/agents.mdx:1-248]() ### ProvidersCommand (`opencode providers`) The `ProvidersCommand` (aliased as `opencode auth` in documentation) manages authentication and configuration for LLM providers [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:130-136](). - **`opencode providers login`**: This command facilitates logging into various LLM providers. It leverages the plugin system's `auth` hook to handle different authentication methods (e.g., OAuth, API keys) [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/providers.ts:39-207](). - It prompts the user for login method if multiple are available, and then for necessary credentials (e.g., API keys, authorization codes) [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/providers.ts:44-92](). - For OAuth flows, it can open a URL for authorization and wait for a callback [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/providers.ts:95-165](). - Credentials are saved to `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:143-144](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/providers.ts:1-210](), [packages/web/src/content/docs/cli.mdx:130-154]() --- ## Error Handling The CLI uses a centralized error formatting system in `FormatError`. It translates internal Effect tags and logic errors into user-friendly strings [packages/opencode/src/cli/error.ts:35-126](). Title: Error Formatting Logic ```mermaid graph TD Error["Caught Error Object"] FormatError["FormatError(input)"] TagCheck{"Check _tag or Name"} Error --> FormatError FormatError --> TagCheck TagCheck -->|ProviderModelNotFoundError| Suggest["Suggest models + 'opencode models'"] TagCheck -->|ConfigJsonError| PathMsg["Report invalid JSON path"] TagCheck -->|ConfigInvalidError| Issues["List Zod/Schema issues"] TagCheck -->|CliError| ExitCode["Set process.exitCode"] TagCheck -->|UICancelledError| Silent["Return empty string (silent)"] Suggest --> UI["UI.error()"] PathMsg --> UI Issues --> UI ``` | Error Tag / Name | Formatted Output Description | |---|---| | `ProviderModelNotFoundError` | Suggests similar models and points to `opencode models` [packages/opencode/src/cli/error.ts:59-70](). | | `ConfigJsonError` | Reports invalid JSON/JSONC in the config file [packages/opencode/src/cli/error.ts:79-83](). | | `ConfigRemoteAuthError` | Explains SSO/Auth expiry for remote configs [packages/opencode/src/cli/error.ts:97-107](). | | `MCPFailed` | Reports failure of a specific MCP server [packages/opencode/src/cli/error.ts:48-51](). | | `UICancelledError` | Silently handles user cancellation (e.g., Ctrl+C in prompt) [packages/opencode/src/cli/error.ts:122-124](). | The entrypoint `fail` hook and `try/catch` block ensure that these formatted errors are printed to `stderr` before the process exits [packages/opencode/src/index.ts:104-135](). The Configuration System in OpenCode manages hierarchical loading and merging of settings from various sources, maintaining clear precedence rules. It is responsible for loading configurations related to providers, agents, tools, permissions, plugins, and UI preferences, balancing flexibility between global, project, and runtime scopes. This page details the hierarchical configuration loading process, the `opencode.json` schema, and configuration precedence rules alongside their implementation, including the v2 design patterns. --- ## Configuration Sources and Precedence OpenCode supports multiple configuration sources that are merged into a unified configuration for runtime. The merging respects a strict order of precedence where later sources override specific keys from earlier ones but preserve non-conflicting keys. The precedence order of configuration sources (from lowest to highest priority): ```mermaid graph TB Remote["Remote Config
.well-known/opencode"] Global["Global Config
~/.config/opencode/opencode.json"] Custom["Custom Config
OPENCODE_CONFIG env var"] Project["Project Config
opencode.json"] OpenCodeDir[".opencode Directories
.opencode/ (agents, commands, plugins, skills, etc.)"] Inline["Inline Config
OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT env var"] ManagedFile["Managed File Config
System-wide opencode.json"] ManagedMacOS["macOS Managed Preferences
ai.opencode.managed.plist"] Remote --> Global Global --> Custom Custom --> Project Project --> OpenCodeDir OpenCodeDir --> Inline Inline --> ManagedFile ManagedFile --> ManagedMacOS style ManagedMacOS stroke-width:2px ``` ### Precedence Rules Summary | Priority | Source | Description | Key Code Entities | Configuration Loading Implementation The loading process is orchestrated inside `Config.Service` which provides reactive access to the merged config per project or instance context [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:124-135](). ### Data Flow: Config Resolution ```mermaid graph TD Start["Config.Service.get()"] Start --> Auth["Auth.Service.all()"] Auth --> RemoteLoop["fetchRemoteJson()"] RemoteLoop --> MergeRemote["mergeConfigConcatArrays()"] MergeRemote --> LoadGlobal["globalConfigFile()"] LoadGlobal --> MergeGlobal["mergeDeep()"] MergeGlobal --> LoadProject["ConfigPaths.projectFiles()"] LoadProject --> MergeProject["mergeDeep()"] MergeProject --> LoadDirs["ConfigPaths.directories()"] LoadDirs --> ProcessDirs["resolveLoadedPlugins()"] ProcessDirs --> Finalize["normalizeLoadedConfig()"] Finalize --> Return["Return Info Object"] ``` ### Merging Strategy The function `mergeConfigConcatArrays` is used specifically for fields like `instructions` to ensure that organizational defaults and user preferences are additive rather than subtractive [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:45-51](). For other fields, a deep merge is performed where later sources override earlier ones [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:41-43](). The filename (relative to the agents directory) becomes the agent's ID via `configEntryNameFromPath` [packages/opencode/src/config/agent.ts:22](). - **Frontmatter**: Defines metadata and properties which are parsed into `ConfigAgentV1.Info` [packages/opencode/src/config/agent.ts:26-29](). - **Body**: The markdown content is trimmed and used as the agent's `prompt` [packages/opencode/src/config/agent.ts:27](). **Sources:** [packages/opencode/src/config/agent.ts:11-59](), [packages/opencode/src/config/paths.ts:1-50]() --- ## Configuration API and V2 Evolution OpenCode exposes configuration management through its internal service and the generated V2 SDK. ### SDK Interface (`packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/sdk.gen.ts`) The V2 SDK provides a typed interface for interacting with the server's configuration system via the `config` and `globalConfig` namespaces. | Method | Description | |--------|-------------| | `config.get` | Retrieve current instance configuration [packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/sdk.gen.ts:21-22]() | | `config.update` | Update instance configuration [packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/sdk.gen.ts:25-26]() | | `globalConfig.get` | Retrieve global configuration [packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/sdk.gen.ts:79-80]() | | `globalConfig.update` | Update global configuration [packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/sdk.gen.ts:81-82]() | ### Service Implementation (`packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts`) - `Service.get()`: Returns the current `Info` state [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:125](). - `Service.update()`: Updates the configuration. When writing to disk, it uses `patchJsonc` (built on `jsonc-parser`) to ensure that user comments in `opencode.json` are preserved [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:149-161](). - `Service.invalidate()`: Forces a reload of the configuration and clears cached fibers [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:130](). **Sources:** [packages/opencode/src/config/config.ts:124-161](), [packages/sdk/js/src/v2/gen/sdk.gen.ts:20-85]() --- # Page: Session & Agent System # Session & Agent System

The Session & Agent System is the core conversational runtime of OpenCode. It manages conversation threads (sessions), message and part structures, agent configurations (build, plan, explore, etc.), and the agentic execution loop that orchestrates LLM interactions with tools. This system bridges user input to AI-generated responses through a stateful, event-driven architecture powered by the `Effect` runtime [packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:45-46](), [packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:113-149](). --- ## Architecture Overview The Session & Agent System consists of storage (SQLite database via Drizzle ORM), business logic (session/message/agent managers), and the execution runtime (prompt loop + LLM integration). ### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping This diagram maps high-level system concepts to their specific implementation classes and namespaces in the codebase. Sessions use a descending ULID for `id` to ensure reverse-chronological sorting, facilitating recent-first display in UI components [packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:37-38](), [packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:60-121](). | Field | Type | Description | |--------------|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------| | `id` | `SessionID` | Descending ULID ID uniquely identifying the session | | `slug` | `string` | URL-friendly identifier | | `projectID` | `string` | Links session to a specific project | | `workspaceID`| `string?` | Optionally links session to a workspace | | `parentID` | `string?` | For child/forked sessions referencing parent session | | `directory` | `string` | Path of working directory for the session | | `path` | `string?` | Optional project-relative path | | `title` | `string` | Session display title | | `agent` | `string?` | Agent name driving the session | | `model` | `object?` | Model and provider details used by the session | | `version` | `string` | Session versioning string | | `summary` | `object?` | Contains additions, deletions, files changed | | `cost` | `number` | Cost of session usage (tokens or monetary) | | `tokens` | `object` | Token usage broken down by input, output, reasoning, cache | | `share` | `object?` | Public share URL, if any | | `revert` | `object?` | Snapshot and diff information for revert operations | | `permission` | `Array` | Session-level permission ruleset overrides | | `metadata` | `object?` | Additional custom metadata, opaque | | `time` | `object` | Contains created, updated, compacting, and archived timestamps| ### Session Persistence Data Flow The following diagram shows how session lifecycle operations flow through the system layers from API to database. Title: "Session Persistence Flow" ```mermaid graph LR API["SessionPrompt.Service (session/prompt.ts)"] SessNS["Session.Service (session/session.ts)"] DB["Database (core/database/database.ts)"] Table["SessionTable (core/session/sql.ts)"] API -->|calls| SessNS SessNS -->|executes queries| DB DB -->|writes to| Table ``` **Sources:** - [packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:60-121]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:113-149]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:120-159]() --- ## Message & Part System OpenCode's conversation messages are composed of multiple *parts* rather than a single text blob, enabling rich, structured interaction. ### MessageV2 Structure Messages are represented as objects containing metadata (`Info`) and an array of *parts*, each part representing a unit of content or tool interaction. Assistant messages track token usage and costs to support analytics and billing [packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:80-85](), [packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:87-93](). ### Part Types Each part is discriminated by the `type` field with the following major types used in the system [packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:1-17](): | Part Type | Description | |--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `text` | Standard text content in the message | | `reasoning` | Blocks showing assistant's internal thought processes (for models supporting reasoning) | | `tool` | Represents a tool call with state and output details | | `file` | Attached files or media, with MIME type and URL | | `agent` | Reference to a subagent invocation within the conversation | | `compaction` | Marks where context compaction/summarization took place | | `snapshot` | Captures a snapshot state of the worktree at a given step | | `subtask` | Represents a task delegation or a subgoal handled recursively | This granularity allows tooling results, snapshots, and structured outputs to coexist in a single assistant response. The system handles media injection workarounds for providers (like OpenAI or Bedrock) that have limited support for media in tool results [packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:138-159](). **Sources:** - [packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:1-17]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts:131-160]() --- ## Agent System Agents define the behavioral profile configuring how the LLM interacts with the environment, permissions, and tool usage. ### Agent Configurations Defined by the `Agent.Info` schema, an agent includes descriptive data, mode (e.g., "primary", "subagent"), permissions, and optional prompt and model override [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:35-56](). Out-of-the-box agents include: - **Build Agent**: The default primary agent executing permitted tools, allowing `question` and `plan_enter` permissions [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:141-156](). - **Plan Agent**: Specialized for architectural planning; disallows editing except in explicitly allowed plan files [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:157-182](). - **General Agent**: Intended for complex question answering and multitasking [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:183-198](). - **Explore Agent**: Optimized for codebase exploration, permissive with file read/search tools like `grep` and `glob` [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:199-208](). ### Permission Rulesets Permissions merge across three layers — global defaults, agent-specific rules, and user configuration — to create a final effective ruleset [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:120-153](). Key behaviors: - Default rules allow most actions but require explicit ask/deny on sensitive operations like `doom_loop` or access to external directories [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:120-127](). - Sensitive files like `.env` are set to `ask` by default to avoid accidental exposure [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:131-136](). - Agent-specific overrides may grant or restrict permissions, e.g., `plan` agent denies all edit except specific plan files [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:172-177](). **Sources:** - [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:35-153]() - [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:157-208]() --- ## Execution Loop & Context Management ### The Agent Loop The core conversational workflow is the agent loop which processes each assistant message generation in an event-driven streaming manner. This loop drives the LLM prompt-response cycles, tool executions, and updates to the session state [packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:113-149](), [packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:98-115](). Steps: 1. **Start Processing**: The user prompt or assistant message triggers `SessionPrompt.loop`. 2. **LLM Completion Stream**: The configured LLM model streams text token-by-token and emits structured tool calls [packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:98-115](). 3. **Session Updates**: Intermediate assistant messages with their parts are saved to the database [packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:187-200](). 4. **Tool Calls**: Each tool call is dispatched to the `ToolRegistry`, which manages execution and returns results [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:138-164](). 5. **Result Updates**: Tool output parts update their tool call state with status and result [packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:160-184](). Title: "Agent Loop Execution (SessionProcessor)" ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Loop as SessionPrompt.loop participant Proc as SessionProcessor.Service participant LLM as LLM.Service participant Tool as ToolRegistry.Service participant DB as Session.Service Loop->>Proc: create(input) Proc->>LLM: stream(message) LLM-->>Proc: stream text & tool calls Proc->>DB: save assistant message/parts loop For each Tool Call Proc->>Tool: execute tool call Tool-->>Proc: tool output Proc->>DB: update tool part state end Proc-->>Loop: return Result ("continue", "stop", or "compact") ``` **Sources:** - [packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:113-149]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:160-184]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:98-115]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/processor.ts:187-200]() - [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:138-164]() ### Context Compaction & Truncation When the conversation context exceeds the model's maximum token window, the system performs automatic context compaction to summarize and prune content [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:131-150](). - **Overflow Detection**: Measures current token usage against configured context limits [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:168-178](). - **Turn-based Analysis**: Breaks session messages into user-assistant pairs (turns) and selects recent turns worth preserving based on a token budget [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:87-103](), [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:195-211](). - **Pruning**: Truncates excessive tool outputs to max characters (default 2,000) [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:30-31](). - **Context Injection**: Injects the summary into prompt parts to retain high-level session state while freeing token budget [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:52-60](). ### Retry Policy for LLM Calls A robust retry mechanism guards against transient API failures when interacting with LLM providers. It uses exponential backoff and honors headers like `retry-after` to respect provider rate limits [packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts:36-87](). **Sources:** - [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:30-31]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:87-103]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:131-150]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts:168-178]() - [packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts:36-87]() --- ## Session Summary & Diffing The `SessionSummary` service tracks and computes change metrics resulting from assistant interactions [packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts:75-79](). - **Summarize**: Aggregates counts of file additions, deletions, and changed files for a session message [packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts:102-127](). - **Diff**: Calculates file diffs by comparing the snapshot states between step start and finish parts [packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts:82-99](). - **Snapshots**: The system uses `Snapshot.Service` to track file changes via a shadow git directory [packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts:78](). **Sources:** - [packages/opencode/src/session/summary.ts:75-79]() - This document explains how OpenCode integrates with AI providers, discovers and manages model metadata, and routes requests through the provider abstraction layer. It covers provider configuration, authentication (OAuth, API keys, environment variables), model selection fallback chain, provider transforms, and integration with 20+ LLM services, including OpenCode Zen and Go. --- ## Provider Architecture Overview OpenCode supports a wide range of AI providers through a unified abstraction layer that normalizes API differences while preserving unique provider capabilities such as reasoning effort and prompt caching. In the v2 architecture, the `Catalog` service in `packages/core` provides a centralized state container for managing providers and models. ### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping The following diagram bridges high-level configuration concepts to the specific implementation classes and services in the codebase. (opencode.json)"] AuthIntent["Auth.Service
(Credentials)"] ModelsDev["ModelsDev.Service
(Model Catalog)"] end subgraph "Code Entity Space (Implementation)" ProviderSvc["Provider.Service

The providers' SDK factories are lazily imported and cached in the `BUNDLED_PROVIDERS` map to minimize startup time. | Provider Package | Factory Function | Internal SDK Key | | :-------------------------------- | :------------------------ | :----------------------------- | | `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | `createAnthropic` | `anthropic` | | `@ai-sdk/openai` | `createOpenAI` | `openai` | | `@ai-sdk/google` | `createGoogleGenerativeAI`| `google` | | `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` | `createAmazonBedrock` | `bedrock` | | `@openrouter/ai-sdk-provider` | `createOpenRouter` | `openrouter` | | `@ai-sdk/azure` | `createAzure` | `azure` | | `@ai-sdk/xai` | `createXai` | `xai` | | `gitlab-ai-provider` | `createGitLab` | `gitlab-ai-provider` | | `@ai-sdk/github-copilot` | `createOpenaiCompatible` | `copilot` | | `@ai-sdk/google-vertex` | `createVertex` | `vertex` | | `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | `createOpenAICompatible` | `openaiCompatible` | | `@ai-sdk/mistral` | `createMistral` | `mistral` | | `@ai-sdk/groq` | `createGroq` | `groq` | | `@ai-sdk/deepinfra` | `createDeepInfra` | `deepinfra` | | `@ai-sdk/cerebras` | `createCerebras` | `cerebras` | | `@ai-sdk/cohere` | `createCohere` | `cohere` | | `@ai-sdk/gateway` | `createGateway` | `gateway` | | `@ai-sdk/togetherai` | `createTogetherAI` | `togetherai` | | `@ai-sdk/perplexity` | `createPerplexity` | `perplexity` | | `@ai-sdk/vercel` | `createVercel` | `vercel` | | `@ai-sdk/alibaba` | `createAlibaba` | `alibaba` | | `venice-ai-sdk-provider` | `createVenice` | `venice` | Sources: [packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:107-134](), [packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:30-62]() ### Authentication & Connection OpenCode supports multiple authentication methods for providers: - **API Keys:** Stored locally in `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` after users run the `/connect` CLI command. Managed by the `Auth` service [packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx:18-22](). - **Environment Variables:** Used as a fallback for local development or CI. Key names are normalized (e.g., `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`) [packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts:112-122](). - **Provider Options:** Credentials can be passed directly via the `opencode.json` configuration file under `provider..options.apiKey` [packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts:124-131](). - **OAuth:** Supported for services like GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT (Codex) via plugin-based authentication flows [packages/opencode/src/plugin/openai/codex.ts:154-167](), [packages/opencode/src/plugin/github-copilot/copilot.ts:94-104](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:13-15](), [packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx:18-22](), [packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts:112-131]() --- ## Model Management & Discovery ### Model Discovery Flow The `Provider.Service` acts as a coordinator, merging model definitions from multiple sources into the v2 `Catalog`. Title: Model Discovery and Configuration Precedence ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant CLI as "CLI /models Command" participant ProviderSvc as "Provider.Service" participant CatalogSvc as "Catalog.Service" participant ModelsDev as "ModelsDev.Service" participant ConfigSvc as "Config.Service" participant PluginSvc as "Plugin.Service" CLI->>ProviderSvc: list() ProviderSvc->>ModelsDev: Fetch base catalog ProviderSvc->>PluginSvc: discoverModels() hooks ProviderSvc->>ConfigSvc: Read opencode.json overrides ProviderSvc->>CatalogSvc: transform() model state Note over CatalogSvc: Apply whitelist/blacklist Note over CatalogSvc: Apply model aliases CatalogSvc-->>CLI: Final Model Registry ``` ### Configuration Rules Users can control model availability in `opencode.json`: - **Whitelisting:** Restrict a provider to specific models [packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts:155-166](). - **Blacklisting:** Explicitly exclude broken or expensive models [packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts:168-178](). - **Aliasing:** Create custom names for long model IDs [packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts:180-196](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:21-34](), [packages/core/src/catalog.ts:105-159](), [packages/opencode/test/provider/provider.test.ts:155-196]() --- ## Provider Transform Layer The `ProviderTransform` logic transforms and normalizes the diverse API behaviors of 20+ LLM services into a format the OpenCode `LLM.Service` can use. ### Message Normalization OpenCode performs heavy sanitization on messages before they reach the provider: - **Surrogate Pairs:** `sanitizeSurrogates` replaces invalid UTF-16 surrogates that cause crashes in some LLM APIs [packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:25-27](). - **Anthropic/Bedrock Specifics:** Filters out empty content blocks and empty strings which are rejected by these providers [packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:132-187](). - **Tool Call ID Scrubbing:** Claude models require alphanumeric tool call IDs; OpenCode scrubs them automatically [packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:189-201](). ### Parameter Transformations The `ProviderTransform.options` function handles provider-specific flags: - **Prompt Caching:** Sets `promptCacheKey` for Anthropic and OpenAI to reduce latency and cost [packages/opencode/test/provider/transform.test.ts:44-88](). - **Thinking Modes:** Configures "reasoning" or "thinking" parameters for Gemini 2.0, DeepSeek, and GLM models [packages/opencode/test/provider/transform.test.ts:215-245](). - **Stateless Reasoning:** Sets `store: false` for OpenAI/Azure models to prevent server-side state storage when requesting reasoning content [packages/opencode/test/provider/transform.test.ts:141-157](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:25-201](), [packages/opencode/test/provider/transform.test.ts:44-245]() --- ## Integration with OpenCode Zen & Go OpenCode Zen and OpenCode Go are managed services provided by the OpenCode platform. - **OpenCode Zen:** Curated list of high-performance models verified for agentic workflows. Accessed via the `/connect` command [packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx:87-113](). - **OpenCode Go:** Low-cost subscription access to popular open coding models [packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx:123-151](). These are implemented using standard AI SDK packages but route through the OpenCode Console backend for trial management and provider routing [packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx:119-121](). Sources: [packages/web/src/content/docs/providers.mdx:87-151]() --- ## Summary of Key Classes & Functions | Symbol | File Path | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `Provider.Service` | [packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:21]() | Main coordinator for model discovery and SDK instantiation in v1. | | `Catalog.Service` | [packages/core/src/catalog.ts:62]() | v2 state container for managing providers, models, and default selections. | | `ProviderTransform` | [packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:25]() | Logic for normalizing messages and options across different LLM APIs. | | `LLM.Service` | [packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts:55]() | Core service for streaming LLM responses and managing tool execution. | | `BUNDLED_PROVIDERS` | [packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:107]() | Registry of lazily-loaded AI SDK provider factories. | | `wrapSSE` | [packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:37]() | Wrapper for Server-Sent Events to handle timeouts and stream control. | Sources: [packages/opencode/src/provider/provider.ts:37-134](), [packages/opencode/src/provider/transform.ts:25-62](), [packages/core/src/catalog.ts:62-170](), [packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts:55-58]() --- # Page: Tool System & Permissions # Tool System & Permissions

This page documents the tool registry, built-in tools, the permission system gating tool execution at runtime in OpenCode, tool execution hooks, and file integrity mechanisms. It covers tool definition APIs, multi-layered permission evaluation, and techniques to ensure consistent file operations. --- ## Tool Definition API ### Overview All tools in OpenCode are defined via the `Tool.define` function. This utility abstracts JSON schema parameter validation, typed execution context injection, automatic output truncation, and error wrapping [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:151-169](). Tools are created as `Effect` generators to manage asynchronous dependencies like filesystem, LSP, or permission services. The registry normalizes these into a standard interface that the LLM can consume via JSON Schema [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:114-130](). ### Core Concepts - **Parameters**: Defined with `effect` schema and validated at runtime before execution. If validation fails, a `ToolInvalidArgumentsError` is returned to the LLM with specific details on how to rewrite the input [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:24-34](). - **Execute**: An async function that takes typed parameters and `Tool.Context`, returning an `ExecuteResult`. - **Context**: Carries runtime metadata such as session ID, agent info, and helpers for permission gating [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:36-46](). - **Output Truncation**: The wrapper automatically truncates output using `Truncate.Service` to prevent overwhelming the LLM context [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:131-144](). ### Tool.Context All tool executions receive a `Tool.Context`, which acts as the bridge between the tool implementation and the wider session state: | Property | Type | Description | | :---------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `sessionID` | `SessionID` | The unique identifier for the current session [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:37](). | | `messageID` | `MessageID` | The ID of the message that triggered the tool call [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:38](). | | `agent` | `string` | The name of the agent executing the tool [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:39](). | | `abort` | `AbortSignal` | Signal to handle cancellation of the tool execution [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:40](). | | `metadata` | `Function` | Callback to update tool-specific metadata for the UI [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:44](). | | `ask` | `Function` | Primary interface for requesting permissions [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:45](). | ### Tool Registry The `ToolRegistry.Service` [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:81]() is responsible for discovering and managing all available tools. It aggregates: - Built-in tools (e.g., `read`, `edit`, `bash`) - Plugin-provided tools [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:114-169]() - Custom tools loaded from the `.opencode/tool` directory within the project [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:110-115]() The registry ensures that each tool has a unique ID, a description, and a JSON Schema for its parameters, which is crucial for LLM interaction [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:128-131](). #### Tool Definition and Initialization Tools are defined using `Tool.define(id, initEffect)` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:157-169](). The `initEffect` is an `Effect` that resolves to a `DefWithoutID` object, containing the tool's description, parameters (as an `Effect/Schema` schema), and an `execute` function. The `wrap` function [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:99-148]() within `Tool.define` handles several cross-cutting concerns: - **Parameter Validation**: It decodes the input arguments against the defined `Schema` using `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:121](). If validation fails, it throws a `Tool.InvalidArgumentsError` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:124-128](), providing a user-friendly error message to the LLM. - **Output Truncation**: It automatically truncates the tool's output using `Truncate.Service` to manage context window limits [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:131-144](). - **Execution Spans**: It wraps the `execute` call in an `Effect.withSpan` for observability and tracing [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:145-146](). #### Built-in Tools OpenCode includes a comprehensive set of built-in tools: | Tool ID | Implementation | Description | Parameters | | :------ | :------------- | :---------- | :--------- | | `read` | `ReadTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts:64]() | Reads files/directories. ## Permission System ### Overview The permission system in OpenCode controls what actions agents can perform. It is implemented by the `Permission.Service` [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:41]() and evaluates rulesets to determine if a tool call is `allow`, `deny`, or `ask` (requiring user confirmation). ### Permission Evaluation When a tool is executed, it calls `ctx.ask()` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:45]() with the requested permission (e.g., `read`, `edit`, `bash`) and a pattern (e.g., a file path). The `Permission.Service` then evaluates this request against a hierarchy of rules: 1. **Agent-specific Rulesets**: Each agent (e.g., `build`, `plan`) has a default set of permissions defined in `Agent.Info` [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:35-55](). 2. **User-defined Rules**: Users can configure additional rules in `opencode.json` which are loaded and merged [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:186-198](). 3. **Runtime Approvals**: If a permission is `ask`, the user can approve it "once" or "always". "Always" approvals are added to the `approved` state for the current session [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:144-151](). The `evaluate` function [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:28-37]() determines the final action by finding the last matching rule. If no explicit rule matches, the default action is `ask`. ### External Directory Protection A critical aspect of the permission system is protecting against unauthorized access to files outside the current project's worktree. The `assertExternalDirectoryEffect` function [packages/opencode/src/tool/external-directory.ts:10-50]() is used by file-system tools (`read`, `edit`, `write`, `apply_patch`) to check if a requested path is outside the project. If it is, it triggers a permission request for `external_directory`, requiring explicit user approval. #### Permission Evaluation Flow ```mermaid graph TD subgraph "Natural Language Space" tools. ### File Locking The `EditTool` uses a `Semaphore` to implement file-level locking [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:35-45](). When an `edit` operation is initiated on a `filePath`, a semaphore is acquired. This prevents multiple concurrent `edit` operations on the same file from causing race conditions or partial writes. ### Consistency Mechanisms 1. **Line Ending Normalization**: The `EditTool` detects the line ending style (`\n` or `\r\n`) and applies replacements using the detected style [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:22-34](). 2. **BOM Preservation**: Tools like `edit` and `apply_patch` utilize the `Bom` utility to handle Byte Order Marks (BOMs) [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:126-155](), [packages/opencode/src/tool/apply_patch.ts:115-118](). 3. **LSP Synchronization**: After modification, the `LSP.Service` is notified via `lsp.touchFile()` to re-index the changed file [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:115](). 4. **Binary Safety**: `ReadTool` "sniffs" initial bytes to determine if a file is binary [packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts:182-200](). It refuses to read binary content as text to prevent context pollution. 5. **Instruction System**: The `Instruction.Service` [packages/opencode/src/session/instruction.ts:46]() manages project-specific instructions (e.g., `CLAUDE.md`). Tools integrate with this to ensure agents follow local coding standards. ### Background Subagents The `TaskTool` allows agents to launch subagents in the background using `BackgroundJob.Service` [packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:85](). - **Foreground**: Default; agent waits for subagent result. - **Background**: `background=true` launches asynchronously and returns immediately [packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:25-30](). - **Permission Derivation**: Subagents receive a subset of the parent's permissions via `deriveSubagentSessionPermission` [packages/opencode/src/agent/subagent-permissions.ts:10](). ### CodeMode Package The `packages/codemode` package provides a confined environment for code execution. - **Runtime Isolation**: The `CodeModeTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/code-mode.ts]() uses this to run untrusted code safely. - **Tool Access**: Code running in CodeMode can be granted limited access to host tools via `tool-runtime.ts` [packages/codemode/src/tool-runtime.ts](). - **Verification**: Uses signature verification to ensure code hasn't been tampered with before execution [packages/codemode/test/signature.test.ts](). This page documents the HTTP server implementation and REST API architecture that powers OpenCode's networked functionality. The server provides a comprehensive REST API for managing sessions, projects, configurations, and real-time AI interactions using the Effect-based `HttpApi` framework. ## Purpose and Scope The HTTP server serves as the central networked interface to OpenCode's core functionality. It exposes endpoints for: - **Session Lifecycle**: CRUD operations on sessions, message history, and AI prompting [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/session.ts:79-105](). - **Real-time Updates**: Event streaming via Server-Sent Events (SSE) for UI synchronization [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/event.ts:1-10](). - **Provider Management**: Discovery of LLM models and credential configuration [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/provider.ts:1-10](). - **System Control**: Health checks, upgrades, and global instance disposal [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/control.ts:1-10](). - **Terminal Integration**: WebSocket-based pseudo-terminal (PTY) access for remote shell execution [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/pty.ts:1-10](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/session.ts:79-105](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/event.ts:1-10](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/provider.ts:1-10](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/control.ts:1-10](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/pty.ts:1-10]() ## Server Architecture OpenCode uses a modern, type-safe server architecture built on the **Effect** ecosystem. The server logic is defined using `HttpApi`, which enables automatic OpenAPI generation and unified dependency injection across all routes [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/api.ts:54-75](). The main server entry is in `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts` which sets up listeners and integrates the HTTP API routes [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:139-151](). The server supports two primary execution modes: 1. **Network Mode**: An actual HTTP server bound to a TCP port, using `HttpRouter.serve` to bind the route handlers [packages/opencode/test/server/httpapi-session.test.ts:49-55](). 2. **Local Transport Mode**: A "web handler" interface that runs request handling directly without network overhead, useful for internal calls and testing [packages/opencode/test/server/httpapi-ui.test.ts:53-75](). ### Request Flow and Middleware The server defines a layered middleware stack that applies common functionality like authentication, error handling, CORS, compression, and workspace routing. These components facilitate loose coupling between subsystems (Session, LSP, Config, Tools) and provide real-time state synchronization to clients via Server-Sent Events (SSE). What is the architecture of subagents - are they run in separate processes or in the same process? How does the "task" tool delegate to subagents? What is SubagentType and how is a subagent session created? The subagent system allows primary agents to delegate complex tasks to specialized subagents, which run in their own sessions. Subagents are configured via `opencode.json` or markdown files, defining their `mode`, `model`, `permission`, and other behaviors  . The `task` tool is the primary mechanism for delegating to subagents, creating a new session for the subagent with derived permissions .

## Subagent Creation and Configuration

Subagents are defined in the configuration, typically in `opencode.json` or dedicated markdown files . Key configuration parameters include:
*   `mode`: Set to `"subagent"` to designate it as a subagent  .
*   `model`: Specifies the language model the subagent should use  .
*   `permission`: Defines the tools and actions the subagent is allowed to perform  . This can include specific permissions like `edit` or `bash`, and also `task` permissions to control which other subagents it can invoke .
*   `description`: A brief explanation of the subagent's purpose  .
*   `hidden`: A boolean to hide the subagent from the `@` autocomplete menu, useful for internal subagents .

The `Agent.Info` type represents the information about an agent, including its `name`, `mode`, and `permission` ruleset .

## Subagent Execution and Architecture

Subagents are executed within their own sessions, which are child sessions of the invoking agent's session . This means they run in the same process as the main application, but within a distinct session context. The `task` tool creates a new session for the subagent if `task_id` is not provided, or resumes an existing one if `task_id` is specified  .

The `deriveSubagentSessionPermission` function in `packages/opencode/src/agent/subagent-permissions.ts` is crucial for setting up the subagent's permissions . It combines the parent session's deny rules and `external_directory` rules with the subagent's own defined permissions . This ensures that the subagent operates within appropriate boundaries, potentially overriding some parent restrictions while maintaining its own specific limitations  .

The `TaskTool.execute` function is responsible for initiating the subagent's work . It retrieves the subagent's configuration, derives its session permissions, and then creates or retrieves a session for it . The actual prompt execution for the subagent happens via `ops.prompt` within the `runTask` effect .

Subagents can also be run in the background if the `background` parameter is set to `true` and the `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS` flag is enabled .

## Delegation via the "task" tool

The `task` tool is used by agents to delegate work to subagents . When an agent uses the `task` tool, it provides parameters such as `description`, `prompt`, and `subagent_type` . The `subagent_type` specifies which configured subagent to use .

The `task` tool's `execute` method performs several steps:
1.  **Permission Check**: It first checks if the calling agent has permission to invoke the specified `subagent_type` .
2.  **Subagent Retrieval**: It retrieves the `Agent.Info` for the specified `subagent_type` .
3.  **Session Creation/Resumption**: It either creates a new session for the subagent or resumes an existing one if a `task_id` is provided  .
4.  **Permission Derivation**: It derives the subagent's session permissions using `deriveSubagentSessionPermission` .
5.  **Metadata Update**: It updates the current message with metadata about the subtask, including the `parentSessionId` and the `sessionId` of the new subagent session .
6.  **Prompt Execution**: It then calls `ops.prompt` to execute the subagent's task within its new session .

The `subagent_type` parameter in the `task` tool's `Parameters` schema refers to the `name` of the agent to be used as a subagent  . This name corresponds to the agent configurations defined in `opencode.json` or markdown files  .

A subagent session is created by the `sessions.create` method within the `task` tool's execution flow . This new session is linked to the parent session via `parentID`  and is configured with the subagent's specific `agent` name and derived `permission` ruleset .

## Notes

The provided context does not explicitly detail whether subagents run in separate processes or the same process. However, the creation of new "sessions" and the use of `parentID`  suggest a logical separation within the same application process rather than distinct OS processes. The `packages/core/src/session/execution.ts` and `packages/core/src/session/execution/local.ts` files were mentioned in the prompt but were not provided in the codebase context, so their specific contents regarding process architecture could not be analyzed.

The plugin system in OpenCode allows you to extend its functionality by hooking into various events and customizing behavior. Plugins can be loaded from local files or npm packages and are initialized once per session.   

## Plugin Loading and Initialization 
Plugins are loaded and initialized when the `Plugin.init` function is called, which is part of the `Service` layer for plugins.  

### Loading Sources 
OpenCode supports two primary ways to load plugins:
1.  **Local Files**: You can place JavaScript or TypeScript files in `.opencode/plugins/` (project-level) or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (global). These are automatically loaded at startup. 
2.  **npm Packages**: You can specify npm packages in your `opencode.json` configuration file under the `"plugin"` array.  These packages are automatically installed using Bun at startup and cached. 

### Load Order 
Plugins are loaded in a specific sequence: 
1.  Global configuration (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`) 
2.  Project configuration (`opencode.json`) 
3.  Global plugin directory (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/`) 
4.  Project plugin directory (`.opencode/plugins/`) 

Duplicate npm packages with the same name and version are loaded only once. 

### Initialization Process 
The `layer` constant in `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts` defines the plugin service.  During initialization, it performs the following steps:
1.  Retrieves `EventV2Bridge`, `Config`, and `RuntimeFlags` services. 
2.  Creates a `PluginInput` object containing `client`, `project`, `worktree`, `directory`, and `experimental_workspace` for plugins to interact with OpenCode. 
3.  Loads internal plugins, if not disabled by flags. 
4.  Loads external plugins specified in the configuration using `PluginLoader.loadExternal`. 
5.  Applies each loaded plugin by calling its `server` function (for V1 plugins) or iterating through legacy plugins, collecting their returned `Hooks` objects.  
6.  Notifies plugins of the current configuration by calling their `config` hook. 
7.  Sets up an event listener to trigger the `event` hook for all registered plugins when a bus event occurs. 
8.  Registers a finalizer to call the `dispose` hook on all plugins when the plugin scope is disposed. 

## Plugin Hooks 
Plugins interact with OpenCode through a system of "hooks". These are functions defined within a plugin that OpenCode calls at specific points in its execution.  The `Hooks` interface in `packages/plugin/src/index.ts` defines the available hooks. 

When a hook is triggered, the `trigger` function in `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts` iterates through all registered plugin hooks and executes the corresponding function. 

Here are some examples of plugin hooks:

*   `tool.definition`: Allows plugins to define custom tools. 
*   `tool.execute.before`: Called before a tool is executed, allowing modification of input arguments. 
*   `tool.execute.after`: Called after a tool has been executed. 
*   `command.execute.before`: Called before a command is executed. 
*   `config`: Called once on initialization with the merged configuration. 
*   `event`: Called for every bus event. 
*   `shell.env`: Allows modification of environment variables for shell commands. 
*   `permission.ask`: Used to ask for permissions. 
*   `dispose`: Called when the plugin is being disposed of, allowing for cleanup.

Plugins are loaded per-session.  The `InstanceState` in `packages/opencode/src/plugin/index.ts` manages the state of loaded plugins, including their hooks.  When a plugin is deactivated or the session ends, its associated resources are cleaned up via the `dispose` hook.

A plugin module exports a default (or any named export) function of type `Plugin = (input: PluginInput, options?) => Promise<Hooks>`.  This function receives a context object (`PluginInput`) and returns an object containing the hook implementations. 

### V2 Plugin System 
There is also a V2 plugin system under development, which uses an Effect-based API.  In this system, plugins imperatively register transforms and hooks during setup, rather than returning a `Hooks` object.   Hooks in V2 are registered using `ctx.domain.hook("event.name", Effect.fn(...))`.
