This page documents the tool registry, built-in tools, the permission system gating tool execution at runtime in OpenCode, tool execution hooks, and file integrity mechanisms. It covers tool definition APIs, multi-layered permission evaluation, and techniques to ensure consistent file operations. --- ## Tool Definition API ### Overview All tools in OpenCode are defined via the `Tool.define` function. This utility abstracts JSON schema parameter validation, typed execution context injection, automatic output truncation, and error wrapping [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:151-169](). Tools are created as `Effect` generators to manage asynchronous dependencies like filesystem, LSP, or permission services. The registry normalizes these into a standard interface that the LLM can consume via JSON Schema [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:114-130](). ### Core Concepts - **Parameters**: Defined with `effect` schema and validated at runtime before execution. If validation fails, a `ToolInvalidArgumentsError` is returned to the LLM with specific details on how to rewrite the input [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:24-34](). - **Execute**: An async function that takes typed parameters and `Tool.Context`, returning an `ExecuteResult`. - **Context**: Carries runtime metadata such as session ID, agent info, and helpers for permission gating [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:36-46](). - **Output Truncation**: The wrapper automatically truncates output using `Truncate.Service` to prevent overwhelming the LLM context [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:131-144](). ### Tool.Context All tool executions receive a `Tool.Context`, which acts as the bridge between the tool implementation and the wider session state: | Property | Type | Description | | :---------- | :---------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `sessionID` | `SessionID` | The unique identifier for the current session [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:37](). | | `messageID` | `MessageID` | The ID of the message that triggered the tool call [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:38](). | | `agent` | `string` | The name of the agent executing the tool [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:39](). | | `abort` | `AbortSignal` | Signal to handle cancellation of the tool execution [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:40](). | | `metadata` | `Function` | Callback to update tool-specific metadata for the UI [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:44](). | | `ask` | `Function` | Primary interface for requesting permissions [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:45](). | ### Tool Registry The `ToolRegistry.Service` [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:81]() is responsible for discovering and managing all available tools. It aggregates: - Built-in tools (e.g., `read`, `edit`, `bash`) - Plugin-provided tools [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:114-169]() - Custom tools loaded from the `.opencode/tool` directory within the project [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:110-115]() The registry ensures that each tool has a unique ID, a description, and a JSON Schema for its parameters, which is crucial for LLM interaction [packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:128-131](). #### Tool Definition and Initialization Tools are defined using `Tool.define(id, initEffect)` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:157-169](). The `initEffect` is an `Effect` that resolves to a `DefWithoutID` object, containing the tool's description, parameters (as an `Effect/Schema` schema), and an `execute` function. The `wrap` function [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:99-148]() within `Tool.define` handles several cross-cutting concerns: - **Parameter Validation**: It decodes the input arguments against the defined `Schema` using `Schema.decodeUnknownEffect` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:121](). If validation fails, it throws a `Tool.InvalidArgumentsError` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:124-128](), providing a user-friendly error message to the LLM. - **Output Truncation**: It automatically truncates the tool's output using `Truncate.Service` to manage context window limits [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:131-144](). - **Execution Spans**: It wraps the `execute` call in an `Effect.withSpan` for observability and tracing [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:145-146](). #### Built-in Tools OpenCode includes a comprehensive set of built-in tools: | Tool ID | Implementation | Description | Parameters | | :------ | :------------- | :---------- | :--------- | | `read` | `ReadTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts:64]() | Reads files/directories. Supports offsets, line limits (default 2000), and binary detection [packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts:13-19](). | `filePath`, `offset`, `limit` [packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts:28-36]() | | `edit` | `EditTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:58]() | Search-and-replace modification. Requires `oldString` [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:93-95](). | `filePath`, `oldString`, `newString`, `replaceAll` [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:47-56]() | | `grep` | `GrepTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/grep.ts:20]() | Searches patterns using `ripgrep`. | `pattern`, `path`, `include` [packages/opencode/src/tool/grep.ts:10-18]() | | `bash` | `ShellTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/shell.ts:19]() | Executes shell commands. | `command` | | `task` | `TaskTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:81]() | Delegates to subagents. Supports `background` mode [packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:58-62](). | `description`, `prompt`, `subagent_type`, `task_id`, `background` | | `skill` | `SkillTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/skill.ts:12]() | Loads specialized instructions/workflows [packages/opencode/src/tool/skill.ts:46-61](). | `name` [packages/opencode/src/tool/skill.ts:8-10]() | | `write` | ## Permission System ### Overview The permission system in OpenCode controls what actions agents can perform. It is implemented by the `Permission.Service` [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:41]() and evaluates rulesets to determine if a tool call is `allow`, `deny`, or `ask` (requiring user confirmation). ### Permission Evaluation When a tool is executed, it calls `ctx.ask()` [packages/opencode/src/tool/tool.ts:45]() with the requested permission (e.g., `read`, `edit`, `bash`) and a pattern (e.g., a file path). The `Permission.Service` then evaluates this request against a hierarchy of rules: 1. **Agent-specific Rulesets**: Each agent (e.g., `build`, `plan`) has a default set of permissions defined in `Agent.Info` [packages/opencode/src/agent/agent.ts:35-55](). 2. **User-defined Rules**: Users can configure additional rules in `opencode.json` which are loaded and merged [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:186-198](). 3. **Runtime Approvals**: If a permission is `ask`, the user can approve it "once" or "always". "Always" approvals are added to the `approved` state for the current session [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:144-151](). The `evaluate` function [packages/opencode/src/permission/index.ts:28-37]() determines the final action by finding the last matching rule. If no explicit rule matches, the default action is `ask`. ### External Directory Protection A critical aspect of the permission system is protecting against unauthorized access to files outside the current project's worktree. The `assertExternalDirectoryEffect` function [packages/opencode/src/tool/external-directory.ts:10-50]() is used by file-system tools (`read`, `edit`, `write`, `apply_patch`) to check if a requested path is outside the project. If it is, it triggers a permission request for `external_directory`, requiring explicit user approval. #### Permission Evaluation Flow ```mermaid graph TD subgraph "Natural Language Space" tools. ### File Locking The `EditTool` uses a `Semaphore` to implement file-level locking [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:35-45](). When an `edit` operation is initiated on a `filePath`, a semaphore is acquired. This prevents multiple concurrent `edit` operations on the same file from causing race conditions or partial writes. ### Consistency Mechanisms 1. **Line Ending Normalization**: The `EditTool` detects the line ending style (`\n` or `\r\n`) and applies replacements using the detected style [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:22-34](). 2. **BOM Preservation**: Tools like `edit` and `apply_patch` utilize the `Bom` utility to handle Byte Order Marks (BOMs) [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:126-155](), [packages/opencode/src/tool/apply_patch.ts:115-118](). 3. **LSP Synchronization**: After modification, the `LSP.Service` is notified via `lsp.touchFile()` to re-index the changed file [packages/opencode/src/tool/edit.ts:115](). 4. **Binary Safety**: `ReadTool` "sniffs" initial bytes to determine if a file is binary [packages/opencode/src/tool/read.ts:182-200](). It refuses to read binary content as text to prevent context pollution. 5. **Instruction System**: The `Instruction.Service` [packages/opencode/src/session/instruction.ts:46]() manages project-specific instructions (e.g., `CLAUDE.md`). Tools integrate with this to ensure agents follow local coding standards. ### Background Subagents The `TaskTool` allows agents to launch subagents in the background using `BackgroundJob.Service` [packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:85](). - **Foreground**: Default; agent waits for subagent result. - **Background**: `background=true` launches asynchronously and returns immediately [packages/opencode/src/tool/task.ts:25-30](). - **Permission Derivation**: Subagents receive a subset of the parent's permissions via `deriveSubagentSessionPermission` [packages/opencode/src/agent/subagent-permissions.ts:10](). ### CodeMode Package The `packages/codemode` package provides a confined environment for code execution. - **Runtime Isolation**: The `CodeModeTool` [packages/opencode/src/tool/code-mode.ts]() uses this to run untrusted code safely. - **Tool Access**: Code running in CodeMode can be granted limited access to host tools via `tool-runtime.ts` [packages/codemode/src/tool-runtime.ts](). - **Verification**: Uses signature verification to ensure code hasn't been tampered with before execution [packages/codemode/test/signature.test.ts](). This page documents the HTTP server implementation and REST API architecture that powers OpenCode's networked functionality. The server provides a comprehensive REST API for managing sessions, projects, configurations, and real-time AI interactions using the Effect-based `HttpApi` framework. ## Purpose and Scope The HTTP server serves as the central networked interface to OpenCode's core functionality. It exposes endpoints for: - **Session Lifecycle**: CRUD operations on sessions, message history, and AI prompting [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/session.ts:79-105](). - **Real-time Updates**: Event streaming via Server-Sent Events (SSE) for UI synchronization [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/event.ts:1-10](). - **Provider Management**: Discovery of LLM models and credential configuration [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/provider.ts:1-10](). - **System Control**: Health checks, upgrades, and global instance disposal [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/control.ts:1-10](). - **Terminal Integration**: WebSocket-based pseudo-terminal (PTY) access for remote shell execution [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/pty.ts:1-10](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/session.ts:79-105](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/event.ts:1-10](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/provider.ts:1-10](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/control.ts:1-10](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/groups/pty.ts:1-10]() ## Server Architecture OpenCode uses a modern, type-safe server architecture built on the **Effect** ecosystem. The server logic is defined using `HttpApi`, which enables automatic OpenAPI generation and unified dependency injection across all routes [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/api.ts:54-75](). The main server entry is in `packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts` which sets up listeners and integrates the HTTP API routes [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:139-151](). The server supports two primary execution modes: 1. **Network Mode**: An actual HTTP server bound to a TCP port, using `HttpRouter.serve` to bind the route handlers [packages/opencode/test/server/httpapi-session.test.ts:49-55](). 2. **Local Transport Mode**: A "web handler" interface that runs request handling directly without network overhead, useful for internal calls and testing [packages/opencode/test/server/httpapi-ui.test.ts:53-75](). ### Request Flow and Middleware The server defines a layered middleware stack that applies common functionality like authentication, error handling, CORS, compression, and workspace routing. multiple route groups managed by `HttpApiBuilder`. These groups correspond to different concerns and prefixes: | Path Prefix | Functionality | Implementation | |---|---|---| | `/global` | Global system status, events, logs | `globalHandlers` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:90-90]() | | `/auth`, `/log` | Control plane and authentication | `controlHandlers` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:86-86]() | | `/session`, `/file`| Session management, filesystem ops | `sessionHandlers`, `fileHandlers` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:99-99](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:89-89]() | | `/event` | Real-time server-sent event streaming | `eventHandlers` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:84-84]() | | `/doc` | OpenAPI specification JSON | Exposed via `OpenApi.toSpec` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:151-151]() | Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:82-151]() ## Middleware and Lifecycle ### Authentication Authentication and authorization are enforced through dedicated layers: - `authorizationLayer`: Implements Basic Auth using credentials configured via environment variables (`OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` and `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`) [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/authorization.ts:118-132](). - `ptyConnectAuthorizationLayer`: Specialized authorization middleware for PTY WebSocket connections using one-time tickets [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/authorization.ts:134-150](). - `serverAuthorizationLayer`: Used for global server-level routes and applied to `RootHttpApi` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:139-139](). Authorization tokens may be passed via query parameter `auth_token` or HTTP Basic Auth header. Unauthorized access triggers `401 Unauthorized` with appropriate `WWW-Authenticate` headers [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/authorization.ts:12-83](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/authorization.ts:8-150](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:136-139]() ### CORS Configuration Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) is configured via a middleware wrapping `HttpMiddleware.cors`. It uses a whitelist logic in `isAllowedCorsOrigin` that checks origins against configured allowed origins [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:121-129](). A small accompanying middleware `corsVaryFix` ensures compliant response headers for varying CORS origins [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/cors-vary.ts:1-10](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:121-129](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/cors-vary.ts:1-10]() ### Workspace Routing The `workspaceRoutingLayer` middleware manages routing requests to local or remote workspaces. - It extracts workspace and directory info from URL queries or headers [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/workspace-routing.ts:22-30](). - If a remote workspace is specified, it proxies the request transparently to remote URLs using an `HttpApiProxy` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/workspace-routing.ts:113-146](). - Ensures context typing for instance services to support session isolation across project directories [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/workspace-routing.ts:52-62](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/workspace-routing.ts:22-62](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/workspace-routing.ts:113-146]() ### Error Handling Robust error handling is provided through: - An `errorLayer` catches unhandled exceptions, returning a sanitized 500 Internal Server Error with a unique error reference [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/error.ts:9-36](). - A `schemaErrorLayer` specifically handles schema validation errors from request bodies or parameters, converting them into 400 Bad Request responses [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/schema-error.ts:1-10](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/error.ts:9-36](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/middleware/schema-error.ts:1-10]() ## Real-time Transport Modes ### Server-Sent Events (SSE) The server supports real-time event streaming over SSE through the `EventApi` group. This multiplexes different event types related to sessions, projects, and global state [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/api.ts:81-81](). The `eventHandlers` bridge internal event buses to SSE HTTP responses, providing clients with incremental updates for UI synchronization [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:84-84](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/api.ts:81-81](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:84-84]() ### WebSockets (PTY) Interactive terminal sessions are managed under the `PtyConnectApi` namespace. - Clients first request a one-time connection ticket at `/pty/{ptyID}/token` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/pty.ts:144-150](). - Using the ticket, WebSocket upgrade requests are accepted at `/pty/{ptyID}/connect` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/pty.ts:163-200](). - `WebSocketTracker` monitors all active PTY WebSocket connections for graceful shutdown [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/websocket-tracker.ts:1-10](). Sources: [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/handlers/pty.ts:144-200](), [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/websocket-tracker.ts:1-10]() ## OpenAPI Specification The HTTP REST API is formally defined using the `effect/unstable/httpapi` framework. This provides: - **Typed Route Definitions**: The `RootHttpApi`, `InstanceHttpApi`, and other groups define routes with attached JSON schemas [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/api.ts:54-75](). - **OpenAPI Doc Generation**: The API specification can be dynamically generated via `OpenApi.fromApi(PublicApi)` [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/server.ts:151-151](). - **Legacy Compatibility**: A transformation layer in `matchLegacyOpenApi` normalizes schemas (e.g., stripping optional nulls, fixing circular references) to support existing SDK generation [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/public.ts:82-145](). - **Query Parameter Overrides**: Several query parameters have explicit schema overrides to ensure primitive types (numbers, booleans) in the generated SDK [packages/opencode/src/server/routes/instance/httpapi/public.ts:58-74](). ## Purpose and Scope This page documents OpenCode's event-driven architecture, centered around the `EventV2.Service` and instance-specific bus systems. These components facilitate loose coupling between subsystems (Session, LSP, Config, Tools) and provide real-time state synchronization to clients via Server-Sent Events (SSE). This system is critical for streaming AI responses, updating file tree states, and notifying UIs of background task completions. ## Architecture Overview The event system follows a publish/subscribe pattern where core logic modules publish typed events, and the HTTP server broadcasts these to connected clients.
